question: Where is coffee grown, and how much does Viet Nam grow?

sources.name: FAOSTAT, Crops and livestock products (QCL), bulk download, normalized
sources.licence: CC BY 4.0 (FAO Statistical Database Terms of Use, https://www.fao.org/contact-us/terms/db-terms-of-use/en/)

caveats: These are the figures of the FAOSTAT item Coffee, green, which the atlas ties to 4 crops; they are not for one crop alone.

answer:
Coffee is reported by 79 countries to FAOSTAT, with a total global harvested area of 12,353,073 ha [S1]. The largest harvested areas are in Brazil (1,905,536 ha), Indonesia (1,267,388 ha), Colombia (840,479 ha), Ethiopia (833,661 ha), and Uganda (832,866 ha) [S1].

Viet Nam has a harvested area of 667,148 ha (mean of 2022-2024), making it the 7th largest grower [S1]. Viet Nam is also the world's largest exporter of robusta coffee, accounting for over 40% of total production [S2], with nearly 90% of its coffee area dedicated to robusta [S3].
